question: In the Contact process, why is sulfur trioxide (SO3) dissolved in concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to form oleum (H2S2O7), rather than being added directly to water?
correct_answer: The direct reaction between SO3 and water is violently exothermic and forms an uncontrollable, dangerous mist of tiny sulfuric acid droplets that cannot be easily condensed or contained.
wrong_answers_pool: Sulfur trioxide is completely insoluble in pure water.
Adding SO3 directly to water produces toxic sulfur dioxide gas.
Water causes the reverse reaction to occur, decomposing SO3 back into sulfur.
The reaction with water is endothermic and freezes the reaction vessels.
Oleum is required because it has a lower molecular mass than sulfuric acid.
Water neutralizes the acid instantly into neutral water.
